step: Pin syscall table words 1568..1583 to a reserved, asserted pixel range before GH-21 program-text growth
created_by: oversight session (durability review of GH-18 pfn-5 fix)

problem.current_state: admit_syscall writes the table word 1570 via the pfn-5 pixel window [1312,1328). The mapping lands in trailing zero-padding beyond the program text — it is correct at the CURRENT image size but relies on headroom, not a structural guarantee.
problem.failure_mode: GH-21 (POSIX shim) and GH-22 (driver ABI) add kernel program text and syscall slices. When text grows into the padding, the table-write collides with real opcodes again — and the collision will be a correct-looking write into what used to be padding, i.e. a multi-session regression hunt exactly like today's _pix_write_word incident (commit e3d3c13 defect B).
problem.precedent: The fs window [1024,1280) already has an explicit reserved layout with an engine-exact alias in _pix_write_word branch 1. The syscall table deserves the same contract.

required_fix: Define a reserved TABLE_PIXEL_WINDOW (like the fs window) covering the pixel addresses that words 1568..1583 map to, with an explicit layout comment in baker.py and autoatlas.py.
Add a bake-time assertion (test or StaticVerifier leg) that NO program text assembles into that window — assert it in tests/test_gh18_syscall_abi.py so it guards every future bake.
Verify the pfn-5 [1312,1328) mapping is derived from a constant (not image-size-dependent arithmetic); if it depends on current height, pin the derivation so growing program text cannot move it.
gate: New leg in tests/test_gh18_syscall_abi.py: bake every mode (baseline/admit/paged_dispatch), assert table window pixels are reserved (no opcode text) and admit_syscall write path lands inside the reserved window; full run_gate_gh18.sh stays 13/13+
priority: MUST close before GH-21 starts (roadmap ordering note updated accordingly)
